To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the mitochondrial respiratory chain is an important regulator of innate immune cell function; and 2) the respiratory chain is not just a metabolic hub for ATP synthesis but also a signaling platform that is involved in the regulation of innate immune signaling pathways.
the mitochondrial respiratory chain is a metabolic rheostat that modulates innate immune cell-mediated bacterial clearance, inflammation, and tissue repair.
the mitochondrial electron transport chain is a metabolic rheostat of antimicrobial responses of innate immune cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which mitochondria and the respiratory chain regulate immune cell function.
the question how the ETC and metabolite levels regulate innate immune cell function in the context of infection.
understanding the role of the ETC and metabolite signaling in the innate immune cell biology and how it is altered during infection.

the mitochondrial respiratory chain is not a mere ATP generator, but rather a metabolic rheostat of immune cell function.
the ETC is a metabolic rheostat of immune cell-mediated antibacterials responses.
the ETC is an essential metabolic rheostat that orchestrates innate immune cell responses during infection and inflammation.

the mitochondrial respiratory chain is a metabolic rheostat of immune cell-mediated antibacteria responses.
